about_company.about_long: Himadri Speciality Chemical distils coal tar, a by-product of steelmaking, into coal tar pitch, naphthalene and speciality oils, and makes carbon black from its own feedstock. It has 600,000 MTPA of coal tar distillation and about 250,000 MTPA of carbon black capacity, about 130,000 MTPA of it speciality grades, and a 65% share of India's coal tar pitch market. Pitch is a binder for aluminium smelting and graphite electrodes, and carbon black goes into tyres, rubber, plastics, coatings and inks; it also sells SNF and PCE concrete admixtures and Durofresh naphthalene balls. Carbon materials and chemicals were about 91% of Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue (₹1,539.02 Cr of ₹1,691.43 Cr, derived) and the Others segment, Birla Tyres resale plus mining, about 8.5%; customers outside India took 29.1% of FY26 revenue, up from 18.8% in FY24. Birla Tyres Ltd has been wholly owned since April 2025, but the tyre business itself sits with Dalmia Bharat Refractories (DBRL) and a Himadri subsidiary resells its tyres; in September 2026 the board approved a scheme to demerge that business into Himadri from 1 October 2026, which still needs statutory, creditor and shareholder approvals. In battery materials, a 200 MTPA anode plant started in April 2026 and an LFP cathode plant is being built.
about_company.about_short: Advanced materials & application-driven solutions company, formerly a coal tar derivative processor.

what_changed.text: Revenue from customers outside India grew about 72% from FY24 to FY26, to ₹1,357.58 Cr, while revenue from customers in India slipped about 3%; exports went from 18.8% to 29.1% of consolidated revenue, above the 22.0% of FY23. Himadri has liquid coal tar pitch terminals at Haldia and Mangalore ports and sent its first liquid pitch export from Mangalore, to the Middle East, in November 2025. FY26 revenue also includes the new Others segment (₹274.46 Cr of tyre resale and mining).

about_company.business_intro: Himadri buys coal tar, a by-product of steelmaking, distils it into coal tar pitch, naphthalene and oils, and turns its own oils into carbon black. It sells pitch to aluminium smelters and graphite-electrode makers and carbon black to tyre, plastics, coatings and ink makers, in India and abroad. These carbon materials and chemicals were about 91% of Q2 FY27 revenue; the rest came from reselling Birla Tyres products, mining and a little power.
